title.tl: Ang Pagtatagumpay ng Agham sa Kamatayan

description.en:
The Triumph of Science Over Death, or Scientia, is one of the three statuettes Rizal made while in London. Scientia depicts a woman holding a burning torch standing on a skull completely naked. In 19th century art, nudity symbolized power, purity, invincibility, the moral character to conquer ignorance through enlightenment.

There are several reproductions of this piece: one by Inocencio Gallemit now displayed in Silid Pamana of the Museo ni Jose Rizal in Fort Santiago; another, a big concrete replica known as Lady Med, stands in front of the Fernando Calderon Hall of the University of the Philippines College of Medicine in Manila; yet another replica, by Dr. Genaro Sy-Changco, can be found in Alabang, Muntinlupa City, in the former Biological Production Services Building (now part of Festival Mall).

description.fil:
Ang Triumph of Science Over Death, o Scientia, ay isa sa tatlong estatwilyang ginawa ni Rizal habang nasa London. Inilalarawan ng Scientia ang isang babaeng may hawak na nagliliyab na sulo, nakatayo sa ibabaw ng isang bungo, lubos na hubad. Sa sining ng ika-19 dantaon, sinasagisag ng kahubdan ang kapangyarihan, kadalisayan, kawalang-kayang talunin, at ang moral na katangiang lupigin ang kamangmangan sa pamamagitan ng kaliwanagan.

May ilang reproduksiyon ng piyesang ito: isang gawa ni Inocencio Gallemit na nakatanghal ngayon sa Silid Pamana ng Museo ni Jose Rizal sa Fort Santiago; isa pa, isang malaking replikang semento na kilala bilang Lady Med, ay nakatayo sa harap ng Fernando Calderon Hall ng University of the Philippines College of Medicine sa Manila; at isa pang replika, ni Dr. Genaro Sy-Changco, ay matatagpuan sa Alabang, Lungsod ng Muntinlupa, sa dating Biological Production Services Building (ngayon ay bahagi na ng Festival Mall).

description.de:
Triumph of Science Over Death, auch Scientia genannt, ist eine der drei Statuetten, die Rizal in London schuf. Scientia zeigt eine völlig unbekleidete Frau, die eine brennende Fackel hält und auf einem Totenkopf steht. In der Kunst des 19. Jahrhunderts stand Nacktheit für Macht, Reinheit, Unbesiegbarkeit und die sittliche Kraft, die Unwissenheit durch Aufklärung zu überwinden.

Von diesem Werk existieren mehrere Nachbildungen: eine von Inocencio Gallemit, heute im Silid Pamana des Museo ni Jose Rizal in Fort Santiago zu sehen; eine weitere, eine große Betonreplik namens Lady Med, steht vor der Fernando Calderon Hall des College of Medicine der University of the Philippines in Manila; und noch eine, von Dr. Genaro Sy-Changco, findet sich in Alabang, Muntinlupa City, im früheren Biological Production Services Building (heute Teil der Festival Mall).
